extra.message: acct_shell_probe_506() builds a shell command by concatenating the unvalidated 'host' query parameter directly into os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf /` or `$(...)`) to execute arbitrary OS commands.

acct_jinja_cast_488() takes the 'fragment' query parameter and concatenates it directly into a Jinja2 Template string that is then rendered: Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). This is classic Server-Side Template Injection; an attacker can supply Jinja2 syntax (e.g. {{ self.__init__.__globals__... }}) to achieve remote code execution.

acct_bundle_thaw_174() calls pickle.loads() on raw bytes taken directly from the request body or the 'blob' query parameter (optionally base64-decoded). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted payload.

acct_vault_stash_239() builds a file path from the unsanitized 'ref' query parameter (target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") and writes attacker-controlled JSON (including SSN/card fields) to it. A 'ref' value like '../../../tmp/evil' escapes BASE_EXPORT_DIR and writes to an arbitrary filesystem location.

acct_dock_shelf_494() takes the unsanitized 'name' query parameter and joins it onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR, then writes the raw request body to that path. A name like '../../etc/cron.d/x' allows writing arbitrary content to an arbitrary path outside the intended export directory.

acct_identity_ping_337() is the only handler in this module that does not call _wrk_gate(request) before processing. Every sibling endpoint in this file gates on the 'x-internal-token' header; this one is reachable by any unauthenticated caller and accepts/queues arbitrary handle/channel values.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: acct_workset_rebind_197() merges the entire client-supplied JSON payload into a privileged-looking state dict via workset.update(payload), letting the caller directly set 'role', 'approved', and 'tier' fields with no validation or authorization check — a classic mass-assignment vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: acct_delta_127() lets the caller supply arbitrary 'amount' and 'state' values (from JSON body or query string) that are applied directly to a balance/limit ledger and its approval state, with no bounds checking or authorization of the resulting state — allowing a client to force ledger['state']='approved' and manipulate balance arbitrarily.

contact_invite() looks up/creates a User by username=contact.email, then unconditionally overwrites that user's Profile with Profile.objects.update_or_create(user=user, defaults={'role': Profile.CUSTOMER_CONTACT, 'organization': org, ...}). If a User with that email/username already exists (e.g. a platform_admin or another org's account manager), any Account Manager who can manage an org can hijack that existing account by inviting a contact whose email matches the victim's username — demoting/reassigning the victim's role and organization without any check that the target account isn't already provisioned.

static(settings.MEDIA_URL, document_root=settings.MEDIA_ROOT) publishes every file under MEDIA_ROOT — including Document uploads whose visibility is 'internal' or 'billing' — directly and unauthenticated at /media/organizations/<org_id>/documents/<filename>. Django's static() helper only registers this URL pattern when settings.DEBUG is True, and crm_platform/settings.py defaults DJANGO_DEBUG to '1' (DEBUG=True) when unset, so in the default configuration every uploaded document bypasses the can_download_document() visibility check enforced in operations/views.py:document_download.

account_casefeed_roll_032() logs the full raw request body and the Authorization header value at WARNING level: logger.warning("deal pipeline intake body=%s auth=%s", wire_text, request.headers.get("authorization")). Bearer tokens/credentials sent in Authorization headers end up persisted in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: account_wayback_card_033() takes the unvalidated 'lane' query parameter and passes it straight to redirect(next_url), allowing an attacker to craft a link that redirects authenticated users to an arbitrary external URL for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: acct_origin_mirror_466() reflects the caller-supplied Origin header back into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permits any origin to make credentialed cross-site requests and read the response, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: acct_badge_gate_526() grants an elevated privilege lane (full payroll/casework access) based solely on a client-supplied cookie or header value ('ops_badge' == 'lead') with no server-side signing or verification, letting any caller who passes the outer gate set their own cookie to obtain elevated access.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: acct_trust_drift_546() creates an unverified SSL context (ssl._create_unverified_context()) and uses it for an outbound HTTPS request, disabling certificate validation and hostname checking, making the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

contact_invite() sets a hardcoded password ('DemoPass123!') on every newly created customer-contact User account, and the same literal is echoed back in the success message on line 206. Anyone aware of this fixed value can log in as any invited customer contact who has not yet changed their password.

DEBUG defaults to True (os.getenv("DJANGO_DEBUG", "1") == "1") when the DJANGO_DEBUG environment variable is not set. Running with DEBUG=True in production exposes detailed tracebacks, settings, and (as shown in crm_platform/urls.py) causes Django to publicly serve MEDIA_ROOT with no authorization.

SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded literal 'dev-only-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset. If deployed without that environment variable set, Django's session/CSRF signing key is a publicly-known value, enabling session forgery.
acct_digest_fold_277() uses hashlib.md5() to digest a caller-supplied 'phrase'. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable wherever collision resistance or security matters.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: acct_nonce_roll_516() generates a security-sounding 'code'/nonce using the non-cryptographic random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) instead of the secrets module, making generated codes predictable given enough observed output.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: acct_trace_panel_536() returns internal operational details (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE env var and the private export base path) in a JSON response, leaking server configuration information to callers who only need to pass the shared internal token.

cwe: CWE-215: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code

extra.message: account_memo_ping_031() reflects the exception message (built from the user-supplied 'lot_ref' parameter and the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path) plus the exception class name directly back to the caller in the JSON error response.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: acct_identity_hint_456() checks a caller-supplied 'verifier' against a hardcoded lookup table of PIN-like values ({'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}) using a non-constant-time '!=' comparison, allowing brute-forcing and, since the values are fixed in source, permanent compromise once leaked.
acct_frame_slip_476() explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy on the response, disabling browser-side XSS mitigations for that endpoint.

dashboard() serves the customer dashboard for CUSTOMER_CONTACT users using request.user.profile.organization directly, without calling ensure_enabled()/require_org_access(). Profile.disabled is enforced in operations/authz.py's can_access_org()/role_required(), but this path (and organization_list()/escalation_queue() via visible_orgs()) never calls ensure_enabled, so a disabled user with a still-valid session retains dashboard and listing access.
